content: 1. For preterm and low birth weight infants, a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the duration of exclusive breastfeeding. This study was published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1). 2. Dorling et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare two speeds of increasing milk feeds in very preterm or very low birth weight infants. The findings were published in Health Technology Assessment in 2020 (Volume 24, Issue 18). 3. Victora et al. revisited maternal and child undernutrition in lowand middle-income countries, highlighting variable progress toward addressing this ongoing issue. This work was published in The Lancet in 2021 (Volume 397, Issue 10282). 4. Yang et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the duration of exclusive breastfeeding for preterm or low birth weight infants. The results were published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1). 5. McCarthy et al. reviewed intervention studies on iron supplementation in preterm and low birth weight infants. Their findings were published in Nutrition Reviews in 2019 (Volume 77, Issue 12). 6. Mills and Davies reviewed the use of enteral iron supplementation in preterm and low birth weight infants. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012 (Issue 3). 7. Manapurath et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on enteral iron supplementation in preterm or low birth weight infants. The study was published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1). 8. Wessells and Brown estimated the global prevalence of zinc deficiency based on zinc availability in national food supplies and the prevalence of stunting. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2012 (Volume 7, Issue 11). 9. Hambidge reviewed human zinc deficiency, focusing on its implications and management. This work was published in The Journal of Nutrition in 2000 (Volume 130, Supplement 5). 10. King et al. explored zinc homeostasis in humans, providing insights into its regulation and clinical implications. This study was published in The Journal of Nutrition in 2000 (Volume 130, Supplement 5). 11. Gulani et al. conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials to evaluate neonatal zinc supplementation for preventing mortality and morbidity in breastfed low birth weight infants. The findings were published in Indian Pediatrics in 2011 (Volume 48, Issue 2). 12. Staub et al. reviewed the use of enteral zinc supplementation for preventing morbidity and mortality in preterm neonates. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2021 (Issue 3). 13. Sinha et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on enteral zinc supplementation in preterm or low birth weight infants. The study was published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1). 14. Huey et al. examined the effects of oral vitamin D supplementation on linear growth and other health outcomes in children under five years of age. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2020 (Issue 12). 15. Misra et al. reviewed the management of vitamin D deficiency in children, summarizing current knowledge and recommendations. This work was published in Pediatrics in 2008 (Volume 122, Issue 2). 16. Tan et al. reviewed the use of vitamin D supplementation in term breastfed infants to prevent vitamin D deficiency and improve bone health. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2020 (Issue 12). 17. Specker et al. investigated the effects of race and diet on human milk vitamin D and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. Their findings were published in American Journal of Diseases of Children in 1985 (Volume 139, Issue 11). 18. Zittermann et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials to evaluate serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D response to vitamin D supplementation in infants. This study was published in European Journal of Nutrition in 2020 (Volume 59, Issue 1). 19. Kumar et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on enteral vitamin D supplementation in preterm or low birth weight infants. The study was published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1). 20. Kumar et al. evaluated the effects of weekly vitamin D supplementation on mortality, morbidity, and growth in low birth weight term infants in India up to six months of age. This randomized controlled trial was published in BMJ in 2011 (Volume 342). 21. Brown and Noelle reviewed the immune regulatory functions of vitamin A, providing new insights into its role in health. This work was published in European Journal of Immunology in 2015 (Volume 45, Issue 5). 22. Shenai reviewed the rationale and evidence for vitamin A supplementation in very low birth weight neonates. This study was published in Pediatrics in 1999 (Volume 104, Issue 6). 23. Khwaja and Volpe explored the pathogenesis of cerebral white matter injury in preterm infants, focusing on its underlying mechanisms. This work was published in Archives of Disease in Childhood Fetal and Neonatal Edition in 2008 (Volume 93, Issue 2). 24. Lee and Dammann reviewed the relationship between perinatal infection, inflammation, and retinopathy of prematurity. This study was published in Seminars in Fetal and Neonatal Medicine in 2012 (Volume 17, Issue 1). 25. Darlow et al. reviewed the use of vitamin A supplementation to prevent mortality and morbidity in very low birth weight infants. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016 (Issue 8). 26. Rakshasbhuvankar et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials to evaluate vitamin A supplementation in very preterm or very low birth weight infants. This study was published in American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2021 (Volume 114, Issue 6). 27. Manapurath et al. reviewed the effects of enteral low-dose vitamin A supplementation in preterm or low birth weight infants to prevent morbidity and mortality. This study was published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1). 28. Atkinson et al. investigated macromineral balances in premature infants fed their own mothers’ milk or formula. This study was published in The Journal of Pediatrics in 1983 (Volume 102, Issue 1). 29. Harding et al. reviewed calcium and phosphorus supplementation of human milk for preterm infants. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2017 (Issue 2). 30. Kumar et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on enteral calcium or phosphorus supplementation in preterm or low birth weight infants. This study was published in Pediatrics in 2022 (Volume 150, Supplement 1).
